newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea to supply 600 bln won to banks.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea to supply 600 bln won to banks.

text.p: The Bank of Korea plans to supply 600 billion won to the banking system on Tuesday by allowing local banks to cash in Monetary Stabilisation Bonds ahead of maturity, an official at the central bank said.
He said the money supply was aimed at easing tight liquidity caused by the financial failure of the Hanbo Steel Co.

A finance ministry official said the government would extend up to 100 million won in emergency operating funds to each small and medium-sized firm which has run into trouble because of Hanbo's debt default.
The government also plans to advance releasing funds needed to meet rising cash demands ahead of the Lunar New Year holidays, which fall on February 7-9, he said.
Bond market dealers said they expected money supply ahead of the nation's biggest holidays to exceed four trillion won.
The central bank on Monday allowed local banks to cash in another two trillion won worth of Monetary Stabilisation Bonds, which were originally due to mature on February 10.
The central bank official said commercial banks still held about 1.2 trillion won worth of Monetary Stabilisation Bonds maturing on February 10.
